text: A tool is just a name, a description, and a JSON schema for its arguments. The model never executes anything itself — it requests a call, and your application code is what actually runs it and hands the real result back.

Here's the real shape the Claude API expects: name, description, and an input_schema with type, properties, and required — standard JSON Schema. The description is the single biggest lever over whether the model calls this correctly.

Tool use is two requests, not one. Claude replies to the first with a tool_use block naming the tool and its arguments. Your code runs the real lookup. The second request sends that result back as a tool_result, matched by its tool_use_id, and Claude replies with the final answer.

stop_reason tells your code which case you're in. tool_use means Claude wants a tool run before it can continue. end_turn means it's finished. That one field is what a real agent loop branches on at every step.

Different vendors call this tool use or function calling, but the shape is the same everywhere: name, description, schema, structured result. Next up: the frameworks built on top of this exact mechanism.
